rules: National Polygon Dataset is HM Land Registry's published Index Polygon dataset for England and Wales
on completion of a registered title HM Land Registry produces a title plan in most cases a register and one or more index polygons
title plans and registers record the general position of registered-title boundaries unless an exact boundary has been determined
an index polygon is an index whose purpose is to show the indicative location of a registered title
HM Land Registry index polygons are held in vector format
the title plan and register share the title number and index polygons are linked to registered titles through that title number
index polygons follow Ordnance Survey MasterMap features where those features relate to the ownership boundary
ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in MasterMap
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of National Polygon and have simpler identifier create-date and last-updated attributes
National Polygon Service downloads are updated on the second working day of each month and contain data for the previous month
National Polygon Service complete file contains the current complete dataset including changes during the month
National Polygon Service change-only file contains data changed since the previous monthly release
National Polygon Service validation file is provided to validate a download
Title Descriptor class of title describes the Registrar's confidence in the registered title
each registered title has a unique title number and one class of title
a pending registration application may have a title number while estate and class-of-title information are not yet present
a non-absolute class of title can change following a supported application to upgrade the class
Title Number and UPRN data covers registered properties associated with a UPRN address
a title and UPRN are linked only where an AddressBase address relationship exists
Title Number and UPRN technical specification defines Title_No as a mandatory character field and UPRN as a mandatory integer field
published Title Number and UPRN data includes a last-change date and provides a full file plus validation file without a change-only file
Planning Data coordinate searches use WGS84 latitude and longitude in EPSG:4326
multiple dataset parameters can be supplied and a coordinate query returns entities from any selected dataset whose geometry covers the point
Planning Data geometry filtering accepts Well Known Text and spaces in geometry values must be percent encoded in URLs
Planning Data entity API supports geometry_entity filtering
Planning Data entity API supports geometry_reference filtering
Planning Data entity API supports geometry_curie filtering
geometry_relation supports within equals disjoint intersects touches contains covers coveredby overlaps and crosses
entity API supports offset-based pagination
entity API responses provide navigation links for next previous first and last pages
Planning Data does not provide a batch entity endpoint
portfolio property checks therefore require one entity request per property when using the entity API
the field parameter can limit returned fields
clients are expected to use polite rate limiting
for hundreds of properties or local spatial intersections Planning Data recommends bulk downloads and local processing for a stable snapshot
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in CSV format
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in JSON format
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in GeoJSON format
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in Parquet format and Parquet is suited to large datasets
field overrides can be combined with exclude_field to remove fields from responses
Planning Data entity API supports quality filtering

the current OS Data Hub listing identifies OS Terrain 50 with a July 2026 version date
OS Terrain 50 coverage is Great Britain
OS Terrain 50 grid is supplied in ASCII grid format
OS Terrain 50 grid is supplied in GML format
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in ESRI Shapefile format
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GML format
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GeoPackage format
OS Terrain 50 is also available as vector tiles
OS Terrain 50 is free OpenData
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July
OS Terrain 50 is a Digital Terrain Model representing ground after protruding features such as buildings and trees are removed
OS Terrain 50 grid posts are spaced at 50 metre intervals
OS Terrain 50 contours use a 10 metre vertical interval
OS Terrain 50 documentation reports grid accuracy verified by independent GPS field-checking with a root mean square error of 4 metres
adjacent Terrain 50 grid tiles do not overlap
adjacent Terrain 50 grid tiles do not share common height values on their edges
mean high water and mean low water lines used in Terrain 50 are derived from large-scale Ordnance Survey mapping
mean high and low water grid heights are assigned as constant values for each tile using local tide-table averages
the tidal modelling method can create a small discrete height step between adjacent grid tiles
in permanent tidal water the mean-low-water height is extended to the tile edge
foreshore heights are interpolated between mean high water and mean low water
Terrain 50 contour water features use a waterLevelCategory attribute
Terrain 50 does not generate contours between mean high water and mean low water
Terrain 50 spot heights are selected from the highest source point within each enclosed contour
Terrain 50 interpolated spot heights are not guaranteed to be true summits or the highest real-world points
Terrain 50 spot-height output can contain lower values representing depressions
Terrain 50 spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places
